question:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5aecefb0668e068cf500941372e30aa06b74075c2bd56187be3e14c34779591f.png] 

What is the primary function of the structure 'A' attached to the rough endoplasmic reticulum in the given diagram?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manufacturing proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Structure **'A'** in the diagram represents **ribosomes**, which are the fundamental cellular organelles responsible for **protein synthesis**.
 
• Ribosomes are often found attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**, giving it a distinctive "rough" or granular appearance under an electron microscope.
 
• The primary role of these attached **ribosomes** is to translate **messenger RNA (mRNA)** into **polypeptide chains**, which then enter the **lumen** of the **RER** for proper folding and processing. ***Hence, the option regarding manufacturing proteins is correct.***
 
• These proteins produced on the **RER** are typically destined for **secretion** out of the cell, incorporation into the **plasma membrane**, or for use within **lysosomes**.
 
• Ribosomes function by linking **amino acids** together in a specific order dictated by the **genetic code**, a process known as **translation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**:
 
 
• The **ER** is a continuous membrane system that forms a series of flattened sacs within the **cytoplasm** of **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• It is divided into two types: **Rough ER** (studded with **ribosomes**) and **Smooth ER** (lacking **ribosomes**).
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is primarily involved in the **production of fat molecules** (lipids), **steroids**, and the **detoxification** of metabolic byproducts.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus**:
 
 
• The **nucleus** is the "control center" of the cell and is responsible for **storing genetic material** in the form of **DNA** (Deoxyribonucleic acid).
 
• It coordinates cell activities like **growth**, **intermediary metabolism**, and **reproduction** (cell division).
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**:
 
 
• These are membrane-bound organelles containing **digestive enzymes** (hydrolases) responsible for the **digestion of food particles**, damaged organelles, and foreign substances like **bacteria**.
 
• They are often referred to as the **"suicide bags"** of the cell because they can digest the cell itself if it becomes damaged or dies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery**: **Ribosomes** were first identified in the **mid-1950s** by **George Emil Palade**, who used electron microscopy to observe them as dense particles or granules.
 
• **Structure**: A ribosome is composed of two subunits—the **large subunit** and the **small subunit**—which come together during the process of **protein manufacturing**.
 
• **Composition**: They are chemically composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and dozens of distinct **proteins**.
 
• **Location**: While many are attached to the **Rough ER**, "free" **ribosomes** also exist in the **cytosol**, where they synthesize proteins that function within the **cytoplasm** itself.
